doc.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023

title: His Johnny Smith Gibson guitar
summary: He describes his go-to acoustic-electric Johnny Smith Gibson, ordered by mail in 1961 or 62.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: The guitar players who may watch this interview will say well why didn’t he ask him about what guitar Al prefers? Have you had a guitar of choice throughout your career?

Yeah it had to be the one that I used with Dizzy and I used it with Carmen, I used it with the Playboy Club quartet, I use it almost — it’s an acoustic electric guitar. And that means it’s an acoustic instrument and the pick-up is, there’s no holes in the pick-up. It’s suspended on the neck. So the instrument really has a really wooden sound, a warm, wooden acoustic instrument sound. And it fits with jazz, it fits the thing with Carmen, it fits countless situations. It’s my go-to guitar. And if somebody calls me for a date they’re usually looking for this guitar too. So that is my go to — it’s a Johnny Smith Gibson. It was made I think in 1961 or ’62 and I was the first owner. And I bought it — I ordered it, I didn’t play it, I ordered it from a music store and hoping that it would work in the studio because I needed a good rhythm — I had a thin body Gibson that I used, ES 225, it was thin hollow but it had a not good rhythm sound that I needed sometimes. And so I bought this in the mail. And at first it was like boy the two of us are fighting all the time you know. It’s not giving me what I need here. And I spent a lot of money to get it and eventually I beat it into submission and it came around and it’s still — it’s in my bedroom now. And when I’m on the road with anybody it’s on one of the beds in the room. It’s like out there. It’s always there. It is my go-to.
